data.name: GuideQuickStartTitle
data.value: Quick start

data.name: GuideQuickStartBody
data.value:
1. On a new PC, finish the setup wizard. Audio devices and a writable saving folder are required. Speech and LLM setup can be skipped; recording does not require either.
2. Enable a microphone, computer playback, or both. Select the microphone you use and the speaker/headset receiving the computer sound you want to capture.
3. Choose New Recording for a separate session, then Start recording. Pause and Resume use the same button. Stop finalizes the saved audio.
4. For text, set up a local Whisper model under Settings > Speech, then use Transcribe / resume. Live text and automatic transcription after Stop are optional.
5. Select and configure an LLM for main points. Review any transcript uncertainties when prompted, then continue. You can also write My notes yourself without using AI.
Click the AudioMemo logo at the top-left for Settings, Help & About, the saving folder, and common recording/window commands.

data.name: GuideRecordingTitle
data.value: Audio devices and recording

data.name: GuideRecordingBody
data.value:
Microphone captures the selected input. Computer playback captures sound sent to the selected output endpoint, not every speaker or headset at once. Uncheck unused sources; at least one enabled device must work. Quiet or silent input is still a valid device.
If no device can start, AudioMemo shows a warning rather than creating an empty recording. If only one source fails, it can continue with the other and warn you. Check Windows audio routing, microphone permissions, connections, and mute/volume settings if sound is missing.
Pause excludes the paused time. Stop saves the recording before optional AI work. Changing a device during recording asks for confirmation; a failed replacement keeps the working sources where possible.
Settings > Recording controls the saving folder and WAV/MP3, sample-rate, and channel choices for new recordings. A lossless 48 kHz stereo safety WAV is always retained; MP3 or a custom WAV is generated from it.
Continue recording appends to the selected saved session only after confirmation. Use New Recording when you want a separate file and history entry.

data.name: GuideSpeechTitle
data.value: Live text and final transcription

data.name: GuideSpeechBody
data.value:
Whisper turns saved audio into text locally. An LLM is a separate model used for summaries and uncertainty review; configuring an LLM alone does not enable live text.
Under Settings > Speech, download a speech model and choose the recognition language. Auto-detect, Chinese (Simplified), and English are available. The speech-language selector on the main window is separate from the interface language.
Live text can appear while recording, but model loading and inference add delay. Fast drafts use Base on CPU and need both Base and your selected final model for the later refinement pass.
Enable automatic transcription after Stop to finish the recording's text. If it is off, the saved live draft remains available; use Transcribe / resume later to complete it. Final main points require completed transcription.
A missing model or speech-runtime prerequisite is reported without discarding recorded audio. Complete skipped setup in Settings. Model downloads and software installation require your action; the guide does not start them.

data.name: GuideModelsTitle
data.value: LLM setup and privacy

data.name: GuideModelsBody
data.value:
Open Settings > AI main points to configure the selected provider. The main-window LLM selector asks for setup when a choice is not ready; cancelling keeps a usable previous choice.
Ollama: install Ollama, download a local model, then refresh the model list and test the connection. The setup page supplies installation guidance and model commands. Local summaries do not need cloud transcript-sharing consent.
Copilot CLI: use an installed CLI executable, sign in with its account, choose a supported model, and approve transcript sharing. AudioMemo can read the CLI's configured model.
Doubao, Qwen, and DeepSeek: choose the supported official endpoint/region, configure that provider's API key and model, test it, and approve transcript sharing. Account access, usage limits, and charges belong to the provider.
Normal summaries and uncertainty reviews send text, not audio. Editable My notes are never sent as model input. Optional online speech comparison/re-transcription is different: it uploads selected audio only after its own consent.
Changing the selected LLM does not relabel an old result. Hover over Transcript, Main points, or My notes to see the relevant speech or saved-result model information.

data.name: GuideMainPointsTitle
data.value: Generate and update main points

data.name: GuideMainPointsBody
data.value:
After final transcription, click Update main points beside that pane's title. Automatic and live-summary options are available in Settings. Live summaries are provisional; final main points can include a separate Overall summary at the end.
If uncertainty review is enabled, resolve or deliberately keep the flagged passages before a final summary continues. The summary then uses the approved saved transcript.
A recording that has never been summarized starts immediately. Changed text, speaker corrections, or re-transcription can require a fresh summary. If an already-completed summary still matches, AudioMemo asks before spending another model request; choosing No keeps the result.
Main points use the complete saved transcript, not just selected rows or the visible speaker/search filter. My notes are not included. Review generated names, decisions, and action items rather than treating them as verified facts.
Progress counts transcript batches, not repeated transcription passes. Overall summary is a later request. Elapsed covers the current processing run; Step ETA estimates only the current measurable step.
If processing stops, completed results and checkpoints remain saved. Resume unfinished work or update again as appropriate; an incomplete overall summary does not erase completed main points.

data.name: GuideNotesTitle
data.value: My notes and the Me speaker tag

data.name: GuideNotesBody
data.value:
My notes is your editable, automatically saved notebook for the selected recording. You can use it without an LLM. Existing editable notes, including edits to AI-generated sections, are never sent to the model.
To identify your part in a conversation, right-click a labeled transcript row and choose Mark speaker as me. Only one speaker is tagged per recording. Optional names/nicknames help interpret mentions, but a Me tag is your choice, not verified biometric identity.
For a complete transcript, Update my notes requests an About me section covering that speaker's contributions, mentions by others, commitments, and open questions. It uses the whole transcript with the selected LLM and applicable sharing consent. It does not run merely because you tagged someone or updated general main points.
Only the previous unchanged generated section is replaced. Your surrounding notes stay intact. If that section was edited, removed, or duplicated, AudioMemo asks whether to append a new result instead.
Hover over My notes for the model used by the applied AI section. Full speaker reanalysis can clear the Me tag; check it before generating another personal summary.

data.name: GuideNavigationTitle
data.value: Navigate, search, copy, and replay

data.name: GuideNavigationBody
data.value:
The transcript shows Time, Speaker, and Text. The floating toolbar's Actions menu contains speaker filtering, copying, following the latest text, replay, silence, text correction, search, and online comparison. The buttons on the Transcript title row remain in place.
Scroll upward to stop following new text; Latest or Bottom resumes following. The toolbar stays available for short or empty transcripts, so you can change filters or open search. In narrow panes, Actions remains available while the four navigation buttons are hidden. Drag its dotted grip to move it; the position is remembered.
Drag inside a text cell to select words. Select Time/Speaker rows for row actions; Shift selects a range and Ctrl selects separate rows. Copy all text omits times/names; the annotated copy includes them.
The speaker filter can show selected speakers or Not labeled. Check All speakers to include everyone, or uncheck it to clear the selection. Transcript copy commands respect the active filter; filtering alone does not edit audio or restrict a full summary.
Open transcript search to find text and move between matches. Enter/Shift+Enter in the search field moves next/previous. Open Help & About > Keyboard shortcuts for your current bindings rather than assuming the defaults.
For saved audio, select a range and use Play selected, then pause/resume or stop replay. Playback is local. Hearing another voice in an overlapping interval is normal: a speaker filter does not separate mixed audio.

data.name: GuideReviewTitle
data.value: Review unclear transcript passages

data.name: GuideReviewBody
data.value:
Right-click Transcript > Review unclear transcript to check the complete saved text. It combines explicit uncertainty markers with the selected LLM's text-based review. This can miss errors or flag correct wording; it cannot hear the audio or prove a spelling.
Automatic review is on by default in Settings > Speech. It runs after final transcription and before final main points, not during recording or live text. A completed check with no findings can continue without a popup.
The list shows the original passage, speaker, time, quote, and reason. Replay a passage, edit Corrected text only when needed, and select the corrections you want. Apply selected corrections & continue saves those choices. Keep all unchanged & continue preserves the wording. Cancel applies no unsaved corrections and stops that AI task.
Temporary response-format problems are retried once. Retry review or Resume unfinished review can continue an incomplete check; completed parts are reused when the source and model still match. Incomplete results are not a clean bill of health.
Accepted decisions are remembered for unchanged text. No model-suggested spelling is applied automatically, and editable My notes are never included in this check.

data.name: GuideCorrectionsTitle
data.value: Correct text and speaker assignments

data.name: GuideCorrectionsBody
data.value:
For a finished recording, select Time/Speaker rows and use Edit transcript text. Corrections preserve audio, timing, and speaker metadata. Re-transcribe selection offers a local recognition preview that you can review before saving.
Online comparison is optional and separate from the main-points LLM. Review its selected audio ranges, provider, request count, and consent before uploading. Other voices inside those ranges are also included. Opening a comparison is not permission to upload.
Correct speaker reassigns selected rows to an existing speaker. Merge all applies to all rows of the source speaker, including hidden rows. Renaming a speaker and changing its color are different operations.
Recheck unlabeled speakers uses existing assignments and downloaded local speaker models to examine only unlabeled rows. It does not change already-labeled rows; short or ambiguous speech may remain unlabeled.
Double-click a Speaker cell to set its color, even during AI work. All Not labeled rows share one color without being treated as one identified person.
Remembered vocabulary can help future local recognition. Saving vocabulary is separate from saving transcript edits and does not rewrite older text automatically. Update main points after meaningful text or speaker changes.

data.name: GuideSilenceTitle
data.value: Silence and restore audio

data.name: GuideSilenceBody
data.value:
Select finished transcript rows and choose Silence selected. Review the intervals and explicitly choose Edit this recording or Create a copy. In-place editing avoids another library entry; a separate copy gives you independently browsable versions.
Silencing replaces the selected intervals with equal-length silence and removes their transcript rows. It does not cut time from the recording. Every sound in an interval is muted, including overlapping voices. Review boundaries carefully.
A hidden recovery copy is retained, so silencing is not secure erasure and still needs disk space. Keep the complete recording folder, including .restore-source, for restoration. When sharing muted sound, share the exported audio, not a folder containing recoverable original material.
Right-click Transcript > Show muted rows, or use Restore muted sections. Play original previews the recovery audio without changing anything. Select the rows to restore and confirm; unselected sections stay muted.
Restoration keeps the current recording's timeline and your notes. Old summaries are invalidated by audio edits; update main points afterward. Missing recovery files cannot be recreated from silence, so retain backups.

data.name: GuideLibraryTitle
data.value: Library, import, and export

data.name: GuideLibraryBody
data.value:
Select a recording in the left list to open its saved audio/text/notes. Browsing history does not start AI. Use the recording's context menu for available rename, file, processing, export, or deletion actions; review the selected recordings before any batch operation.
Import audio/video creates a separate session without changing the source file. Common audio files and local videos are supported when their codecs are available. For a video with several audio tracks, choose one. Audio is imported, not video frames or subtitles.
After import, Analyze now is optional. You can keep the saved audio and transcribe later. Missing models are reported rather than downloaded automatically.
Right-click Transcript > Export audio (whole recording) to rebuild that recording's WAV/MP3 output. This is not text-to-speech of main points, and selected rows or filters do not limit the export. Finish recording/AI work before exporting.
Open saving folder or Open files to locate local data. Changing the saving folder changes which library is shown; it does not move old recordings. Back up complete recording folders if you need their notes, transcripts, and recovery history.

data.name: GuideWorkspaceTitle
data.value: Window layout, appearance, and shortcuts

data.name: GuideWorkspaceBody
data.value:
The top-left logo menu provides recording commands, Settings, import, the saving folder, panel visibility, Message history, and Help & About.
Pin or hide the recording list and show/hide Main points or My notes as needed. In narrow windows the recording list may use a temporary preview. Drag the thin dividers to resize panes; these are not separate audio recordings.
Settings > Appearance controls the interface language, theme, fonts, and other display preferences. English and Simplified Chinese are supported. Interface language and speech-recognition language are separate choices.
Right-click the bottom status bar to toggle messages, current LLM, speech model, library size, recording count, and free disk space. The menu stays open for several choices; hiding ordinary messages does not hide warnings.
Help & About > Keyboard shortcuts displays your current saved bindings and their scope. Change them in Settings > Keyboard shortcuts: click a field, press a combination, and Save. Backspace/Delete clears a binding. Conflicting and protected Windows/text-editing commands cannot be assigned.
Run setup / reset in Appearance can rerun onboarding. Read its keep/default-preferences choices; resetting preferences does not delete recordings or downloaded models.

data.name: GuideRecoveryTitle
data.value: Long recordings, safe close, and backups

data.name: GuideRecoveryBody
data.value:
Allow about 0.69 GB per hour for the safety WAV, plus exports, edits, and recovery copies. Prefer a local NTFS/ReFS drive with free space. FAT32 cannot hold a file above 4 GB. Very large WAVs use RF64 and need a compatible player or an MP3 export.
Keep power and audio connections stable. AudioMemo requests that Windows stay awake, but manually sleeping, closing a laptop lid, or shutting down can still interrupt capture. No program can recover audio that never reached storage.
Closing during recording or AI/export work asks for confirmation. Confirmed safe close finalizes capture, preserves published results, and remembers unfinished processing. Let cleanup finish instead of force-ending the process.
On the next launch, Resume unfinished work can continue with the recorded choices and current credentials/consent. Declining starts no AI; you can resume later from the recording's menu. Unsaved edits in a correction dialog are not silently applied.
After an unexpected exit, select the interrupted recording and use Recover WAV. It can repair saved length/header information, not reconstruct missing or corrupt audio.
Each recording folder holds audio, session metadata, transcript, summaries, and notes.md. Back up the complete folder, including hidden recovery data. On another PC, rerun device/model setup and authentication; copying the executable alone does not install models or transfer working credentials.

data.name: GuideTroubleshootingTitle
data.value: Troubleshooting and message history

data.name: GuideTroubleshootingBody
data.value:
No audio device: reconnect or refresh devices, enable at least one valid source, and check Windows permissions/routing. Computer playback must point to the output actually receiving the sound.
No live text: check Live text, the local speech-model download, language, and runtime prerequisites in Settings > Speech. Wait for model loading. Recording can still be saved without text.
Slow AI: model size and available CPU/GPU memory matter. A smaller suitable model may be faster. Step ETA is an estimate for one step, not the entire job; a request without measurable progress may show Estimating.
Review waiting: the AI task may be waiting for your decision, not doing more inference. Apply selected corrections, keep the original deliberately, retry/resume an incomplete check, or cancel. An empty incomplete list does not mean no uncertainties exist.
Controls unavailable: some actions need a completed saved recording or must wait for recording, saving, editing, or AI work to finish. Read the status or warning rather than forcing the process to close.
Open Message history from Help & About, the logo menu, or the status bar to see when, why, and what the app reported. Copy relevant error details for troubleshooting, but avoid sharing credentials or private recording information. History is stored locally and is not sent to AI.
